_policy: A test listed here is known to depend on something other than its own code (wall-clock timing, or the order in which the parallel test runner schedules classes). When it fails inside a tier run it is re-run ONCE, alone and serially: if it passes it is reported as FLAKY and does not block; if it fails again the gate fails. Tests that are not listed are never retried, so an intermittent failure of a concurrency or data test is always a hard failure. Entries expire (60 days at most) and need an owner and a reason.

entries.reason: Asserts that 200 calls of ensure_contrast() finish in under 2.0 s of wall-clock time. Observed failing once on a GitHub-hosted 2-core runner running 4 parallel test workers (run 43165890401) and passing in every other run, including 6/6 local runs, three of them with all CPUs saturated. The threshold is a property of the test, not of the product.
entries.resolution: Measure CPU time (time.process_time) instead of wall-clock time, or raise the threshold. A test-only change in its own branch.

entries.reason: Order dependence of the test suite. The failure seen on GitHub (run 43167434726, 4 parallel workers) is Store.DoesNotExist for slug 'akhlaghi' inside setUp(): a TransactionTestCase scheduled earlier in the same worker flushed the database, which deletes the store that a data migration created, and this class only re-creates it AFTER each of its tests (_fixture_teardown), not before its first one. Whether the test is hit depends on how the runner distributes classes over workers, i.e. on the worker count and on which test modules exist in the commit. The test passes alone (3.11 and 3.12), as a class, and in the full tenant tier with 8 workers on Python 3.12. It is the same class of defect as the serialized_rollback pollution fixed in commit b4bcb15d (15 classes); this class was not among them.
entries.resolution: Test-only fix: make the _akhlaghi() helper get-or-create the store (as _fixture_teardown already does) or mark the class serialized_rollback = True using apps.core.tests.serialized_rollback. Separate branch; not part of the release infrastructure.
